info.name: Primer Client Session API Payments API API

params.name: status
params.description: Filter payments by their status.

params.name: payment_method_type
params.description: Filter payments by their payment method type.

params.name: processor
params.description: Filter payments by their payment processor.

params.name: currency_code
params.description:
Filter payments by their payment currency.
e.g. use `USD` for US dollars.

params.name: from_date
params.description: Return only payments from this date (inclusive).

params.name: to_date
params.description: Return only payments up to this date (inclusive).

params.name: order_id
params.description: Return payments related to this order ID.

params.name: min_amount
params.description: Return payments of this amount minimum (inclusive).

params.name: max_amount
params.description: Return payments of this amount max (inclusive).

params.name: customer_id
params.description: ID of the customer that has made the payment.

params.name: merchant_id
params.description: ID of the merchant involved in the payment.

params.name: customer_email_address
params.description: Email of the customer that has made the payment.

params.name: last_4_digits
params.description: Last 4 digits of the card used for the payment.

params.name: paypal_email
params.description: Paypal email address associated with the payment.

params.name: klarna_email
params.description: Klarna email address associated with the payment.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of payments to return per page.

params.name: cursor
params.description: If results are paginated, pass the `nextCursor` to access next page.

items.docs:
<p/>

Retrieve a list of your payments.

Results are paginated, they will only return up to 100 payments maximum.
To access the next page of result, set the `cursor` query parameter to the value of `nextCursor` in
your current result payload. Use `prevCursor` to go back to the previous page.

**Note:** this endpoint returns a list of
summarized payments. Not all payments attributes are present. You can use
the query parameters to filter payments. You can separate multiple query parameters with t

<p/>

Create and authorize a payment for a given customer order. You
should provide a payment method token here to avoid PCI implications.

If only a payment method token is passed, the values passed with the Client Session is used to determine the amount, currency etc.
Note: `amount`, `currencyCode` and `orderId` are required during payment creation. Make sure to pass these fields when creating a client session, or if not yet available, when creating a payment.

params.name: id
params.description: ID of the payment to authorize.

items.docs:
<p/>

Manually authorize a payment using a provided processor. This is useful if you want to authorize a payment without a workflow action.
The processor merchant ID must be provided which can be found on the [Integrations page](https://dashboard.primer.io/integrations).
The processor name is optional but it must be provided if your account has multiple processors configured which share the same merchant IDs.

params.name: id
params.description: ID of the payment to capture.

items.docs:
<p/>

fully capture, or partially capture funds from the authorized payment, depending
on whether your selected payment processor supports it. The payment will
be updated to `SETTLED` or `SETTLING`, depending on the payment method type.

params.name: id
params.description: ID of payment to cancel.

items.docs:
<p/>

Provided the payment has not reached `SETTLED` status, Primer will
send a "void" request to the payment processor, thereby cancelling the payment
and releasing the hold on customer funds. Upon success, the payment will transition
to `CANCELLED`. The payload is optional.

params.name: id
params.description: ID of payment to refund.

items.docs:
<p/>

Issue a full or partial refund for a previously settled payment. By default, the full amount
will be refunded unless a specific amount is provided for a partial refund.

If the payment was partially captured multiple times, you can specify which capture to
refund by using the transaction event ID. Refer to the `transactions.events` array in the
payment object to find available transaction event IDs (when the appropriate `expand`
parameter is passed).

params.name: id
params.description: ID of payment to resume.

items.docs:
<p/>

Resume a payment's workflow execution from a paused state. This
is usually required when a Workflow was paused in order to get further information
from the customer, or when waiting for an asynchronous response from a third
party connection.

params.name: id
params.description: ID of payment for adjusting authorization.

items.docs:
<p/>

Adjust authorized amount. This is only possible if `authorizationType` was set to 
`ESTIMATED` when the payment was created, and the mechanism is supported by the payment method.

params.name: id
params.description: ID of payment to retrieve.

items.docs:
<p/>

Retrieve a payment by its ID.
